frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The hand-to-hand conveyance of a discrete thing: causing (or effecting) a concrete or reified item to pass into a possessing hand/grasp. The root supplies the "manual transfer of a thing into a hand" — neutral as to direction (into-another's-hand = give, into-one's-own-hand = take/reach); direction is contributed by the derivational form, not by the root.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The hand-to-hand conveyance of a discrete thing: causing (or effecting) a concrete or reified item to pass into a possessing hand/grasp. The root supplies the "manual transfer of a thing into a hand" — neutral as to direction (into-another's-hand = give, into-one's-own-hand = take/reach); direction is contributed by the derivational form, not by the root.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all three form-families the invariant is a thing changing hands. The Form IV verb أعطى and the verbal noun عطاء dominate (13/14) and are transparently "hand X over into someone's possession": al-Kawthar conveyed to the Prophet (108:1 أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ); Paradise as عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, a conveyance "not cut off" (11:108); the Lord's عَطَآء dispensed to both groups and never مَحْظُورًا/withheld (17:20 ×2); every created thing handed its own form (20:50 أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ); Solomon's هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا to dispense freely (38:39); the disbeliever who أَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰٓ — "handed over a little, then held back" (53:34), where the very contrast with withholding shows the root = the act of passing a thing across; the reckoned عَطَآء of the Hereafter (78:36); the pious مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ (92:5); يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰٓ (93:5); the charity given/not-given فَإِنْ أُعْطُوا۟ ... وَإِن لَّمْ يُعْطَوْا۟ (9:58 ×2). Crucially 9:29 يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍ makes the "hand" literal ("hand over the jizya out of hand") and shows the root does NOT require benefaction — here the transfer is upward tribute, not a gift. The lone Form VI, 54:29 فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ ("he took in hand/reached out, then hamstrung"), reverses the vector to take-into-one's-own-hand, confirming that the root itself encodes the hand-conveyance while the form fixes its direction.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions: (a) FORM — Form IV is causative "cause-a-thing-to-reach-a-hand" = give/bestow; Form VI تعاطى is take/reach-into-one's-own-hand; the verbal noun عطاء reifies the transferred thing or the act. Strip these and the direction/valence disappear, leaving bare hand-conveyance. (b) CONSTRUCTION — the double-object frame (أعطى + recipient + item, e.g. أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ) supplies recipient+item slots; مِنْ in أُعْطُوا۟ مِنْهَا supplies partitive source; عَن يَدٍ in 9:29 externally names the hand. (c) PARTICIPANTS — God-as-giver (108:1, 20:50, 93:5, 78:36, 17:20), human giver (92:5, 53:34), human payer (9:29), taker/villain (54:29): the giver/taker identity is not in the root. (d) CONTEXT — eschatological reward (11:108, 78:36), legal tribute (9:29), narrative (38:39, 54:29, 108:1): all contextual. Residue after subtraction = "a thing conveyed manually into a hand/possession."
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 54:29 (word_ref 54:29:3:2) فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ — the only occurrence that is not "giving": the villain of Thamud "took in hand / reached out" for the deed (or the sword) and then hamstrung the she-camel. It is the hardest case because its direction is the opposite of the other thirteen (taking, not giving) and its object is diffuse. It reconciles cleanly once the residue is stated as direction-NEUTRAL hand-conveyance: Form VI supplies the "into-one's-own-hand" vector, so the root's own contribution (a thing brought across into a grasp) is still fully recoverable. Indeed this occurrence is the best internal proof that "giving" is form-supplied, not root-supplied.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest rival is "bestowal / benefaction — bestowing a benefit or gift." It fits the reward and gift verses well (108:1, 11:108, 17:20, 38:39, 78:36, 93:5). But internal evidence arbitrates against it: (1) 9:29 يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ is tribute paid *upward* under subjugation (وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ) — a burden, not a benefaction; (2) 53:34 أَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا paired with withholding is grudging, not gracious; (3) 54:29 تَعَاطَىٰ is taking, and destructive. "Benefaction" therefore over-specifies valence that several occurrences contradict, whereas "hand-conveyance of a thing" (valence- and direction-neutral) covers all 14. The data thus favors the neutral-conveyance hypothesis.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) root Atw ء ت ي (آتى Form IV "give/bring, grant") — very high overlap in the "give" sense (both used for divine grants). Distinction: آتw foregrounds bringing/making-come-to (delivery, wide and often abstract — kingdom, book, wisdom, zakat), while ETw foregrounds the HAND and physical handing across, and — uniquely — is directionally reversible (تعاطى = take/reach), a move آتw does not make. The عَن يَدٍ collocation (9:29) and تعاطى (54:29) are internal signatures ETw has and آتw lacks. (2) wahaba وهب "grant gratuitously" — specifies gratuitousness/gift-status the ETw jizya case contradicts. (3) razaqa رزق "provide sustenance" — specifies the provisioned life-support content. Falsifiability: the hand-conveyance hypothesis is falsified if an ETw occurrence denoted a purely abstract bestowal with no thing-passing-into-possession/grasp sense AND was directionally fixed as give-only such that تعاطى-type reversal were impossible — i.e., if the root behaved identically to آتw with no residual "hand/grasp" component. No such occurrence appears in the data.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — manual hand-to-hand conveyance of a discrete thing into a possessing grasp — is recoverable in every one of the 14 occurrences, and no occurrence must be forced. It is surface-transparent in the 13 give/gift occurrences and is directly corroborated by the literal "hand" in 9:29 (عَن يَدٍ). The one Form VI case (54:29) does not break unity but actually confirms that direction (give vs. take) belongs to the form while the root carries only the neutral conveyance. I decline STRONG for two honest reasons: (a) the root's contribution is directionally UNDERdetermined (give in Form IV, take in Form VI), so the "determinate direction" criterion for STRONG is not met; and (b) the distinction from its near-synonym آتw (ء ت ي) is real but not razor-sharp — it rests on the "hand/grasp + reversibility" component rather than a wholly separate concept. Unity is robust with light abstraction, hence MODERATE rather than STRONG, and well clear of WEAK/UNRESOLVED. No occurrence remains unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation sweep of all 14. Transparent-give core (108:1, 38:39, 53:34, 92:5, 93:5, 9:58x2) is unimpeachable. عطاء-as-bestowal cases (11:108, 17:20x2, 78:36) are mass/ongoing bestowal rather than discrete objects handed across; absorbed by the 'reified item' hedge but within root sense, not breaks. 9:29 (jizya عن يد) is the candidate's best datum, not a weakness: literal hand + compelled upward tribute correctly refutes any 'gift/benefaction' reading and discriminates against وهب/منح. Hardest case 54:29 تعاطى (sole Form VI, the direction-neutrality showcase): contested — some exegetes read 'undertook/ventured' (no thing-into-hand), but the root-faithful reading عطا=تناول (reach out hand and take) is lexically grounded, so it survives non-circularly and even supplies the 'take' reflex distinguishing ETw from آتى (Aty IV). REAL FAILURE = 20:50 (أعطى كل شيء خلقه): endowment of a creature's constitutive form is not conveyance of a separable pre-existing item into a possessing hand — nothing changes hands, the thing doesn't pre-exist its form. Only rescued by reifying intrinsic nature as a conveyed object, which is the ad-hoc/over-broad move the 'concrete OR reified' hedge smuggles in; the specific 'hand/grasp' component collapses to bland 'bestow' here. Distinctiveness holds against وهب (non-benefaction, 9:29) and آتى (take-reflex, 54:29), though the آتى 'give' overlap is the weak edge and 'hand' is metaphorical in endowment cases. Falsifiable (clear failure line: no thing conveyed / no possession change); no occurrence cleanly meets it, but 20:50 sits on the over-breadth boundary. Hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, not SUPPORTED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ — Form IV: al-Kawthar conveyed/handed over to the Prophet; direct into-another's-hand transfer.
عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ — verbal noun: a conveyance/dispensing 'not cut off'; the thing passed into possession, residue present.
عَطَآءُ رَبِّكَ ... مَحْظُورًا — the Lord's dispensing that is never withheld; hand-conveyance of the thing intact.
مِنْ عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَ — supply drawn 'from the Lord's giving'; thing passed into the recipient's grasp.
أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ — each thing handed its own created form; metaphorical bestowal bridged by the root's own 'conveying a thing into possession' logic.
هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا — 'our gift' Solomon may dispense freely; verbal noun of the thing conveyed.
أَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ — 'handed over a little, then held back'; explicit contrast with withholding foregrounds the act of passing a thing across.
فَتَعَاطَىٰ — lone Form VI: 'took in hand / reached out'; vector reversed to take-into-own-hand, root's hand-conveyance preserved (direction from form).
عَطَآءً حِسَابًا — the reckoned 'gift' of the Hereafter; verbal noun, thing conveyed into possession.
مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ — the pious 'one who gave'; absolute Form IV, act of handing over.
يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ — 'your Lord will give you'; direct into-your-hand conveyance.
يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍ — 'hand over the jizya out of hand'; literal hand-transfer, upward tribute confirms root does not require benefaction.
وَإِن لَّمْ يُعْطَوْا۟ مِنْهَا — 'if they are not given from it'; passive of the thing not conveyed into their hand.
فَإِنْ أُعْطُوا۟ مِنْهَا — 'if they are given from it (the charity)'; passive Form IV, thing handed to them.
